title: Section equivalence and canonical derived push-pull adjunctions
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, and take their small pro-étale sites small relative to module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], also writing $R_T$ for its reconstructed section-ring sheaf. Let $E_T:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}(\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\operatorname{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ be the fixed equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the ordinary module operations, their specified adjunctions, and geometric composition comparisons of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Use the unbounded derived functors of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] internally and the canonical ringed derived pullback and K-injective direct image [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] externally. Then termwise $E_T$ induces an equivalence $D(E_T)$, preserving and reflecting K-injective complexes and identifying K-injective resolutions. The canonical comparisons give $D(E_X)Lf^*_{\mathrm{int}}\cong Lf^*_{\mathrm{sec}}D(E_Y)$ and $D(E_Y)Rf_{*,\mathrm{int}}\cong Rf_{*,\mathrm{sec}}D(E_X)$, compatible with their resolution comparison transformations. They identify the independently derived adjunctions, including units and counits. For composable scheme morphisms these comparisons identify the derived pullback composition isomorphisms obtained from the ordinary geometric compositors and their adjunction mates.

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors; Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 07A6, lemma-adjoint, and 0FPI, lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility. Internal/section comparison of these canonical constructions.

proof.text: Write $C(E_T)$ for degreewise application and $Q_T$ for localization; subscripts int and sec distinguish the two module categories. The fixed $E_T$ is an additive exact equivalence by [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport]. Its inverse is additive and exact too. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to both functors. This gives $D(E_T)$ and the factorization $D(E_T)Q_{T,\mathrm{int}}\cong Q_{T,\mathrm{sec}}C(E_T)$. The ordinary equivalence unit and counit applied degreewise are chain isomorphisms (naturality makes them commute with the differentials). By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] they descend to unit and counit isomorphisms for the two derived functors; the triangle identities descend because they hold degreewise. Thus $D(E_T)$ is an equivalence induced by the specified $E_T$.

An additive equivalence is right adjoint to its inverse, and the inverse is exact by Step 1. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applied to $E_T$ and then to its inverse proves preservation and reflection of K-injectivity. Exactness preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so a K-injective resolution $a:M\to I$ becomes $C(E_T)a:C(E_T)M\to C(E_T)I$, again a K-injective resolution [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Conversely apply the inverse and the equivalence unit. The smallness and commutativity hypotheses give unbounded K-injective resolutions in the section category by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], hence also internally by this inverse construction. Comparison maps and homotopies of resolutions are sent degreewise to comparison maps and homotopies: the equation $u-v=dh+hd$ is preserved by additivity. A quasi-isomorphism between any two such K-injective targets is a homotopy equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], so these identifications also give the canonical resolution identifications in the derived categories.

For each $f$ put $P_f=f^*_{\mathrm{int}}$, $S_f=f^*_{\mathrm{sec}}$, $U_f=f_{*,\mathrm{int}}$, $V_f=f_{*,\mathrm{sec}}$. The ordinary comparison theorem [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] gives $c_f:E_XP_f\cong S_fE_Y$ and $r_f:E_YU_f\cong V_fE_X$, identifying their specified adjunctions. These are the comparisons retained in [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]: $r_f$ is the identity on underlying sections, and $c_f$ is its normalized adjunction comparison. The internal pullback is exact for every scheme morphism by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main], and hence the section pullback is exact by the exactness-transport clause of the ordinary comparison theorem. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives the degreewise descents with $\varphi:F_DQ\cong QC(F)$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] each $(F_D,\varphi)$ is a left derived functor (right Kan extension along $Q$). By the universal property both specified total left derived pullbacks are therefore canonically isomorphic to these descents, compatibly with their comparisons $\epsilon$, and $\epsilon_M$ is invertible for every complex $M$. In particular every complex computes these left derived functors, including the K-flat resolutions used by the independently specified constructions. Each of $U_f,V_f$ preserves K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], since its left adjoint is exact.

Apply [lem-derived-exact-equivalence-squares] with $B=\operatorname{Mod}_{R_Y}(\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathrm{Ab}))$, $H=\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X}(\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathrm{Ab}))$, $B'=\operatorname{Mod}(R_Y)$, $H'=\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$, $E=E_Y$, $G=E_X$, and the four ordinary functors and comparisons of Step 3. The supplied universal derived pairs are precisely the total derived pairs in the statement, so the lemma supplies natural isomorphisms $\lambda_f:D(E_X)LP_f\cong LS_fD(E_Y)$ and $\rho_f:D(E_Y)RU_f\cong RV_fD(E_X)$ with both comparison-transformation equations. For example, if $\beta_{\mathrm{int}}:Q_YU_f\to RU_fQ_X$ and $\beta_{\mathrm{sec}}:Q_YV_f\to RV_fQ_X$, the right equation, suppressing localization factorization isomorphisms, is $\rho_{f,QI}\,D(E_Y)(\beta_{\mathrm{int},I})=\beta_{\mathrm{sec},C(E_X)I}\,Q_Y(r_{f,I})$. On K-injective $I$ the two beta maps are isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]; hence $\rho_f$ there is exactly the class of $r_{f,I}$ under the resolution identifications. The left equation similarly says that $\lambda_f$ is the class of $c_f$ on complexes under Step 3's exact-pullback identifications. These are comparisons with the independently supplied functors, not definitions of either functor by transport.

proof.text: For either ordinary adjunction $P_f\dashv U_f$ or $S_f\dashv V_f$, the termwise Hom bijection descends to homotopy categories by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. The adjunction of [lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization] has the representative formula below: use the class of all complexes as the left resolving class, since the pullbacks are exact by Step 3 and therefore invert all quasi-isomorphisms. This class contains every object (its resolving representative can be the identity); the target has K-injective resolutions by Step 2. In notation $P\dashv U$ on either side, for every chain map $t:P(M)\to I$, the derived transpose of $Q(t)\circ\epsilon_M$ is $\beta_I\circ Q(t^\flat)$, where $\epsilon:LP\,Q\to QP$ is the left derived comparison and $t^\flat$ is the ordinary termwise transpose. For arbitrary $M$ and K-injective $I$, this formula accounts for every derived morphism: $\epsilon_M$ is invertible by exactness, and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies maps into $QI$ with homotopy classes of chain maps. On the other side $UI$ is K-injective by Step 3, so the same statement applies to the transposed Hom set. Thus the formula compares the full derived adjunction, not merely its values on degree-zero objects. It remains to see that this is the specified adjunction. Both specified derived adjunctions are the ones derived from the ordinary adjunction, whose counit satisfies $\varepsilon'_{QI}\circ LP(\beta_I)=Q(\varepsilon_I)\circ\epsilon_{UI}$ for every complex $I$ by [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived]. The formula above with $t=\varepsilon_I$, $t^\flat=1_{UI}$ says the normalized counit satisfies the same equation. For K-injective $I$, $\beta_I$ is invertible, so the two counits agree at $QI$; every object is isomorphic to such a $QI$, so by naturality they agree everywhere, and an adjunction between fixed functors is determined by its counit.

The ordinary adjunction comparison [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] says for every chain map $t:P_fM\to I$ that the section transpose of $C(E_X)(t)\circ c_{f,M}^{-1}:S_fC(E_Y)M\to C(E_X)I$ equals $r_{f,I}\circ C(E_Y)(t^\flat)$. It holds degreewise and hence on homotopy classes by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Apply localization and insert the left and right comparison equations of Step 4. The formula in Step 5 then gives precisely the same equality for the two derived Hom bijections under $\lambda_f,\rho_f$. Every target is represented by a K-injective complex by Step 2, so naturality proves this equality for all derived objects. Units are transposes of identities and counits are inverse transposes of identities; consequently the specified units and counits agree. Explicitly, for $A\in D_{\mathrm{int}}(Y)$ and $N\in D_{\mathrm{int}}(X)$ the equalities are
$$\eta_{\mathrm{sec},D(E_Y)A}=RV_f(\lambda_{f,A})\circ\rho_{f,LP_fA}\circ D(E_Y)(\eta_{\mathrm{int},A}),$$
$$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sec},D(E_X)N}=D(E_X)(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{int},N})\circ\lambda_{f,RU_fN}^{-1}\circ LS_f(\rho_{f,N}^{-1}).$$
This establishes equality of the independently derived adjunction structures under the specified comparisons.

Let $h=g\circ f$. Write $d_{g,f}:U_gU_f\cong U_h$ and $e_{g,f}:V_gV_f\cong V_h$ for the ordinary geometric direct-image compositors retained in [def-pd-section-module-operations-data] and [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp]. Their comparison square is
$$r_h\circ E_Z(d_{g,f})=(e_{g,f}E_X)\circ(V_g r_f)\circ(r_g U_f).$$
Indeed $r_f,r_g,r_h$ are identities on sections. At a site object over $Z$, both sides take a section over the iterated fibre product to its section over the canonically isomorphic fibre product with $X$; the isomorphism is the geometric fibre-product associator in $d,e$. Restrictions and scalar actions agree because all the maps are the retained coefficient maps. The ordinary pullback compositors are the adjunction conjugates of $d^{-1},e^{-1}$ by [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] and the retained section convention. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], with the adjunction comparisons of Step 3, to the displayed right square. The bijection of mates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives the left square: $c_h$ followed by the section pullback compositor equals the internal pullback compositor followed by $c_g$ and $c_f$ with the appropriate whiskerings. Thus the specified ordinary pullback compositors commute with the section comparisons.

proof.text: All ordinary pullbacks in Step 7 are exact by Step 3. By [prop-sfb-module-left-derived-upper-star-comp], the internal derived pullback compositor is induced by precisely that ordinary pullback compositor. By Step 3 ([lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]), degreewise application computes the section derived pullbacks too; thus their canonical derived composition comparison is the localization of the ordinary one. Apply degreewise application and then localization to Step 7's left square. The left comparison equations from Step 4 identify its sides with $\lambda_h$ and the pasted $\lambda_f,\lambda_g$, giving the required derived composition square. Equality on all complexes implies equality of the natural transformations by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Finally, [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] and the unit/counit equations of Step 6 show that taking the adjunction mates of this square gives the same right square under $\rho$. Explicitly a mate is $\eta$ followed by the whiskered given map and then the whiskered $\varepsilon$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; substituting Step 6's identities cancels the comparison isomorphisms in adjacent factors. Hence the comparisons identify the derived composition isomorphisms with their specified adjunction mates as well.
